story: The dove and the rainbow (SERIES.md episodes 10 and 11 in one Short; arc 3, The Flood)
people: The scoffer died in the flood, and Noah says nothing until Genesis 9:25 (a curse scene, left for later), so the opposing power is the flood itself and the only speaker is God: His lines (Genesis 9:11 at the open, Genesis 8:16 at the turn, Genesis 9:13 at the payoff) are a deep voice-over over the sea, the sunlight and the rainbow, with no person on screen. Noah (DRAFT) appears by reference in three shots (wardrobe 'ark' at the door, 'before-the-flood' on the hillside after it) and never speaks; his hands at the window and his family are anonymous, seen from behind or in silhouette. No establishing shot. The Keeper only for the insight, the comment question and the close. This plan passes plan_check only once Noah is APPROVED.
beats: structure bible-story-short (script.beats): cold_open s-open (the opposing power on screen: the ark alone on the flood, God's Genesis 9:11 voice-over, the promise He makes after the flood (Genesis 9:8-11), laid over a world still under water as a flash-forward); stake and open loop (eight people, no shore: how long can they hold on?); escalation in three rising steps of the waters against the family's hope, acted, each ending on a hook (God remembered Noah, the ark grounds on Ararat, but still only water; the raven never returns and the dove finds no rest; seven days more, the olive leaf, and the dove does not come back); God speaks Genesis 8:16 (s-go, voice-over: go forth of the ark), then the acted climax s-forth and s-family-out (Noah steps out onto dry ground) carrying Genesis 8:18; the altar (Genesis 8:20-21: man's heart is evil from his youth, yet no more curse); payoff (God's Genesis 9:13 over the rainbow, the family and Noah look up); keeper_close (insight: the flood did not change the human heart, and God promises mercy anyway; comment question; part 11).

narration.text: He would promise that later. For now, a world under water. Eight people in one ark, no shore anywhere. How long can they hold on?
And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark:
Remembered. Not because God forgot, but because the next move was His. A wind began to blow across the water.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
The hull scraped rock and stopped. But outside, still nothing but water, stretching to every horizon.
Months later Noah opened the window. The raven flew out and never came back to him.
And he sent forth a raven, which went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth.
But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark,
He reached out his hand and drew her back in. Still only water. Still no place to land.
Seven more days. Then he let her go again, and they watched the sky until evening.
And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
A single green leaf. Somewhere out there, something was growing again. Seven days later, the dove did not come back at all.
And Noah went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him:
Over a year inside. Now his feet touched dry ground, and every creature followed him out.
And Noah builded an altar unto the Lord; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
and the Lord said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth;
The first rainbow, over a washed world. A promise hung in the sky.
Most readers miss this. The flood did not change the human heart. God says it is still evil from youth, and promises mercy anyway.
When you see a rainbow now, what will you remember? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part eleven tomorrow: The tower of Babel.
